correctness.rationale: The law of one self-avoiding ancestral path is a disjoint exact sum. Conditioning on a successful path yields an exact recursion for a second voter with explicit success-to-root, success-to-known-path, unseen-vertex and self-collision alternatives. These exactly reconstruct first and second moments for all permitted network sizes and direct-voter probabilities, verified by 100136 complete small-n assignments with exact arithmetic. At the square-root critical scaling, logarithmic expansions and Gaussian product domination yield the first ancestral-path density and the second path conditional success limit, giving the double integral for the joint event. The limiting covariance is strictly positive because the absorption probability strictly increases with an already-known successful path is strictly increasing in a. Monotone coupling completes the two off-critical regimes. No finite experiment is substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The fresh contribution is the strictly positive critical limiting variance and non-self-averaging represented fraction at direct-voting probability inverse-square-root order. The 2016 study computes only the no-guru event; the 2021 paper treats fixed positive probabilities for truth tracking; the 2023 complete-digraph paper gives a substantially more general FINITE partition recursion, which already determines finite-law moment information. It does not state or directly derive the singular square-root critical covariance asymptotic; the present theorem requires a two-exploration collision scaling. Related earlier bipartite expected-representation results give the same first-moment crossover in a balanced case, so no originality is asserted for the crossover mean alone. Equivalence to classical random-mapping asymptotics remains possible.
residual_risks: Classical random-mapping theory may contain equivalent square-root rooted-versus-cyclic basin second-moment scaling under a different name.
The 2023 complete-digraph finite partition recursion gives, in principle, full finite-law coverage; the original element here is the singular asymptotic non-self-averaging, not any finite subcase.
Bibliographic searches cannot establish global uniqueness; an unindexed or unpublished equivalent result remains possible.

value.rationale: The model measures a practically motivated, natural election-wide invariant: the share of initial voting weight that survives unresolved delegation cycles. The result determines a sharp critical participation scale but, more significantly, proves that the represented fraction remains intrinsically random at that scale, with an explicit order-one variance and an example standard deviation about 0.265 at c=1. A mean-only participation estimate fails to describe election-level risk in large populations; the second-ancestral-line correlation has mathematical content not reducible to substituting numbers into a known fixed-parameter model. The variance theorem is not a textbook normalization or arbitrary finite slice, and no full limit law is asserted.
